findings.issue_text: TopicUser.find_by result can be nil causing NoMethodError and 500 error when user has no TopicUser row for the topic (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:103-110), which is common for category-watch email recipients who never visited the topic, making the unsubscribe link crash for exactly its target users

Shared unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url} but only UserNotifications#send_notification_email supplies it; other senders using add_unsubscribe_link: true (e.g., digest mailer) will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument at build time and their emails stop being sent (config/locales/server.en.yml:1852-1855, lib/email/message_builder.rb:66)

No graceful handling for logged-out users clicking the unsubscribe link: current_user.id is used with no nil check and filter configuration unclear, so logged-out users either get a 500 error or a login bounce without completing the unsubscribe action (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98-112)
unsubscribe_url may be a relative path ("#{url}/unsubscribe" without Discourse.base_url prefix) causing broken links in email clients if Topic#url is relative (app/models/topic.rb:719-721)

State-mutating unsubscribe action performed on a plain GET with check_xhr skipped and no CSRF token, so link prefetchers or cross-site links can silently mute topics (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98, config/routes.rb:438-439)

Toggle semantics don't match promised behavior: users at regular level get fully muted (stronger than stopping notifications) while watching users only drop to regular and keep receiving reply/mention emails, contradicting the 'You will stop receiving notifications' message; exclusive > comparison on regular looks like a boundary slip (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105-109)

Full TopicView construction happens before the slug/redirect check in the unsubscribe action (topics_controller.rb:98-101), wasting heavy multi-query work on every slug-mismatched request such as the slug-less t/:topic_id/unsubscribe route or stale email links; only topic.slug is needed for the redirect

The unsubscribe action performs a full topic render (perform_show_response serializing the entire post stream with cooked HTML and participants) as a side effect of a notification-level toggle, and the Ember route fetches a full topic-view JSON just to display a title and notification-level dropdown; a lightweight update-and-redirect flow would avoid duplicating the expensive show path

Possible NoMethodError 500 on the unsubscribe click path: TopicUser.find_by in topics_controller.rb:103-105 has no nil guard, so tu.notification_level raises if no TopicUser row exists for the user/topic pair (edge cases like races, purged records, or notification types bypassing TopicUser.change)

The topic-specific unsubscribe_url is interpolated into the List-Unsubscribe header, which is semantically wrong for mail processors expecting one-click unsubscribe to stop all mail of that type; providers may keep sending other-topic emails after treating the user as unsubscribed

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicUser.find_by result can be nil causing NoMethodError and 500 error when user has no TopicUser row for the topic (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:103-110), which is common for category-watch email recipients who never visited the topic, making the unsubscribe link crash for exactly its target users

adjudication_records.issue_text: Shared unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url} but only UserNotifications#send_notification_email supplies it; other senders using add_unsubscribe_link: true (e.g., digest mailer) will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument at build time and their emails stop being sent (config/locales/server.en.yml:1852-1855, lib/email/message_builder.rb:66)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the shared `unsubscribe_link` server translation to include `%{unsubscribe_url}` (config/locales/server.en.yml). `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` unconditionally does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true (lib/email/message_builder.rb), so any email built with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but without `unsubscribe_url` in `template_args` will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`. This diff updates `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` to pass `unsubscribe_url`, but the diff does not show any other call sites being updated, so existing ones could now break at build time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No graceful handling for logged-out users clicking the unsubscribe link: current_user.id is used with no nil check and filter configuration unclear, so logged-out users either get a 500 error or a login bounce without completing the unsubscribe action (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98-112)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code unconditionally calls `current_user.id` when looking up `TopicUser` (`tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])`). If the unsubscribe URL is visited while logged out (common for email links), `current_user` can be `nil`, causing a `NoMethodError` (500). The diff does not show any login-enforcing filter for `unsubscribe`, only `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`, so the nil case is not guarded in this action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: unsubscribe_url may be a relative path ("#{url}/unsubscribe" without Discourse.base_url prefix) causing broken links in email clients if Topic#url is relative (app/models/topic.rb:719-721)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Topic#unsubscribe_url` as `"#{url}/unsubscribe"` (app/models/topic.rb). In the email flow, `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` passes `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` into the template args, and the server locale string renders it directly in a markdown link without adding `Discourse.base_url` (config/locales/server.en.yml + lib/email/message_builder.rb). Elsewhere in the same email template, links are explicitly prefixed with `Discourse.base_url` (app/views/email/notification.html.erb uses `Discourse.base_url` + `post.url`), which is strong evidence these model URL helpers can be relative. If `Topic#url` is relative like `post.url`, the unsubscribe link in emails will be relative and can break in email clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: State-mutating unsubscribe action performed on a plain GET with check_xhr skipped and no CSRF token, so link prefetchers or cross-site links can silently mute topics (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98, config/routes.rb:438-439)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that **mutates state** by toggling and saving `TopicUser.notification_level` (`tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!`) while being exposed via **plain GET routes** (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`). The controller also explicitly skips `:check_xhr` for `:unsubscribe` (`skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`). Because this is a GET, Rails CSRF protections typically won’t require a token, so cross-site links or prefetchers could trigger the state change unintentionally. This matches the finding and is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Toggle semantics don't match promised behavior: users at regular level get fully muted (stronger than stopping notifications) while watching users only drop to regular and keep receiving reply/mention emails, contradicting the 'You will stop receiving notifications' message; exclusive > comparison on regular looks like a boundary slip (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105-109)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the new toggle logic (`if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` then set to `:regular` else set to `:muted`) does not consistently “stop receiving notifications” as the new copy claims. Users at `:tracking`/`:watching` are only downgraded to `:regular` (not muted), meaning the endpoint is not a true unsubscribe/stop-notifications action for those states. This behavior is directly shown in `app/controllers/topics_controller.rb` (new `unsubscribe` method) and conflicts with the newly added messaging in `client.en.yml` / `server.en.yml` that implies notifications will stop for the topic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Full TopicView construction happens before the slug/redirect check in the unsubscribe action (topics_controller.rb:98-101), wasting heavy multi-query work on every slug-mismatched request such as the slug-less t/:topic_id/unsubscribe route or stale email links; only topic.slug is needed for the redirect

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff shows `@topic_view = TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` is executed before the redirect guard `if slugs_do_not_match || (!request.format.json? && params[:slug].blank?)`. Given the newly added slug-less route `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`, requests without a slug will always hit that redirect condition, meaning a full `TopicView` is built even when only the topic URL/slug is needed to redirect. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/efficiency concern rather than a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The unsubscribe action performs a full topic render (perform_show_response serializing the entire post stream with cooked HTML and participants) as a side effect of a notification-level toggle, and the Ember route fetches a full topic-view JSON just to display a title and notification-level dropdown; a lightweight update-and-redirect flow would avoid duplicating the expensive show path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which builds a full `TopicView` (`@topic_view = TopicView.new(...)`) and then calls `perform_show_response`, whose HTML branch preloads/serializes the full topic view (`store_preloaded("topic_#{@topic_view.topic.id}", ...topic_view_serializer)`) and renders `:show`. On the client, the new Ember route `topic-unsubscribe` calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` and `topic.updateFromJson(json)` even though the template only needs a title string and a notifications dropdown. This matches the finding as an efficiency/architecture concern (expensive show-path reuse for a notification toggle), but it is not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Possible NoMethodError 500 on the unsubscribe click path: TopicUser.find_by in topics_controller.rb:103-105 has no nil guard, so tu.notification_level raises if no TopicUser row exists for the user/topic pair (edge cases like races, purged records, or notification types bypassing TopicUser.change)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil`, and the subsequent `tu.notification_level > ...` will raise `NoMethodError` if no `topic_users` row exists for that user/topic. The diff adds no nil guard or fallback creation path, so this is a real 500 risk on that route.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The topic-specific unsubscribe_url is interpolated into the List-Unsubscribe header, which is semantically wrong for mail processors expecting one-click unsubscribe to stop all mail of that type; providers may keep sending other-topic emails after treating the user as unsubscribed

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `unsubscribe_url` being added to email template args (e.g., `user_notifications.rb` passes `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`, and `server.en.yml` uses `%{unsubscribe_url}` inside the *body* `unsubscribe_link` text that gets cooked and substituted into `html_override`). However, nothing in the shown diff indicates that `unsubscribe_url` is interpolated into the `List-Unsubscribe` header itself; the only header-related change visible is in the spec adding `unsubscribe_url` to the builder options while still only asserting header presence, not contents. Therefore the claim about the header semantics cannot be verified from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: topics_controller.rb unsubscribe action has nil deref on TopicUser — TopicUser rows are created lazily, so users notified via category watching may have no row and clicking the unsubscribe link raises NoMethodError on nil.notification_level, causing HTTP 500

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil`, but the code immediately calls `tu.notification_level` and later `tu.save!` without any nil-guard. This is a concrete nil-dereference risk in the diff that would raise `NoMethodError` and produce a 500 when no `TopicUser` row exists for that user/topic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: topics_controller.rb unsubscribe action has nil deref on current_user — the GET action is reachable by anonymous users, so email links clicked without an active session hit current_user.id and return 500 instead of a login redirect

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `TopicsController` explicitly adds `:unsubscribe` to `requires_login` (`requires_login only: ... :unsubscribe`), so the `unsubscribe` GET action should not be reachable by anonymous users. While the action does call `current_user.id`, the diff-grounded evidence indicates a login requirement is enforced, contradicting the finding’s premise that anonymous users can hit it and trigger a nil deref.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: config/locales/server.en.yml shared unsubscribe_link translation gained a required unsubscribe_url interpolation, but only UserNotifications#send_notification_email was updated — other MessageBuilder callers with add_unsubscribe_link: true (digests, invites, plugins) will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and silently drop emails

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` always renders `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `add_unsubscribe_link: true`, so any caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` but does not provide `unsubscribe_url` in `opts` would raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`. The diff only shows one production caller updated (`UserNotifications#send_notification_email` now passes `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`) and the spec adjusted similarly, but the claim about other existing callers (digests/invites/plugins) is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: app-route-map.js.es6 new topicUnsubscribe route is shadowed by the earlier-registered topic resource — /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe matches topic.fromParamsNear, resolving as a topic view with nearPost='unsubscribe' instead of entering the topicUnsubscribe route, so the feature's UI never appears

adjudication.rationale: In the shown `app-route-map.js.es6`, the existing `topic` route is `this.resource('topic', { path: '/t/:id' }, function() { this.route('fromParamsNear', { path: '/:nearPost' }); });`, which recognizes URLs like `/t/<id>/<nearPost>`. The new route is `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` (three segments after `/t`). That URL cannot match `/t/:id/:nearPost` because it has an extra path segment, and `topicBySlug` (`/t/:slug`) also cannot match longer paths. From what the diff shows, there is no earlier `/t/:slug/:id/:nearPost` pattern that would interpret `nearPost='unsubscribe'`, so the claimed shadowing is not supported by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: topics_controller.rb unsubscribe GET endpoint performs a state-changing write (mutates TopicUser#notification_level) with no confirmation token — email prefetchers and mail scanners can silently mute topics without user consent

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new GET route and controller action `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (`get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` / `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) which *mutates state* by changing `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!`. This endpoint is linked from notification emails via `%{unsubscribe_url}` and `post.topic.unsubscribe_url`, and it explicitly skips `check_xhr` for `:unsubscribe`, making it reachable by normal GET requests. There is no confirmation step or token in the URL/params shown in the diff, so automated email link scanners/prefetchers could trigger the GET and silently change the user’s topic notification state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Topic#unsubscribe_url builds the link via string interpolation of Topic#url which may return a relative path, producing broken/unresolvable relative links in email clients; the new spec itself passes a relative '/t/1234/unsubscribe' which doesn't rule this out

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Topic#unsubscribe_url` as `"#{url}/unsubscribe"` and wires it into emails (`unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` in `user_notifications.rb`, consumed by the `unsubscribe_link` translation via `MessageBuilder`). The new spec explicitly supplies a relative `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"`, so it does not assert that email links are absolute/resolvable. While the diff doesn’t show what `Topic#url` returns (relative vs absolute), the review point about not ruling out broken relative links in email clients is a concrete gap in the added coverage and contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `tu` from `TopicUser.find_by` can be nil, causing NoMethodError → 500 on the unsubscribe endpoint instead of a graceful response

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil`. The subsequent access `tu.notification_level` (and later `tu.save!`) will raise `NoMethodError` when no `TopicUser` row exists for that user/topic, causing a 500 instead of a graceful response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Same code path crashes with NoMethodError if `current_user` is nil (anonymous hit) unless the before_filter list enforces login — needs verification

adjudication.rationale: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action does call `current_user.id` (would crash if `current_user` were nil), but this diff explicitly adds `:unsubscribe` to the `requires_login` list (`requires_login :show, ... :bookmark, :unsubscribe`), indicating the before-filter/login enforcement was updated for this action. Based on the diff alone, the review finding’s premise (not enforcing login) is not supported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsubscribe is a state-changing, non-idempotent GET with toggle semantics; reloads/prefetchers can silently change notification level

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` routed to `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which **mutates** `TopicUser.notification_level` and saves (`tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!`). The logic is explicitly toggle-like (`if tu.notification_level > regular then regular else muted`), making repeated GETs non-idempotent (reload/back/prefetch can silently flip the state). This is a real behavior introduced by the diff and can cause unintended notification-level changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: First click while watching/tracking only drops to regular, so user still receives notification emails despite the page promising to stop notifications

adjudication.rationale: The new unsubscribe page promises "You will stop receiving notifications" (client.en.yml `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications`), but `TopicsController#unsubscribe` only lowers `tu.notification_level` to `:regular` when the user is currently `:tracking`/`:watching` (`if tu.notification_level > ...[:regular] then ...[:regular] else ...[:muted]`). That means the first click from tracking/watching does not mute the topic, so notifications can still occur, contradicting the page text.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Browser reload of the unsubscribe page flips muted back to regular, silently re-subscribing the user

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, reloading the unsubscribe URL re-runs the same toggle logic: if `tu.notification_level > :regular` it is set to `:regular`, otherwise it is set to `:muted`. After the first visit sets the user to `:muted` (or leaves it muted), a reload hits the `else` branch again and keeps it `:muted`; there is no code in the diff that would flip a muted topic back to regular on page reload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Ember unsubscribe route's model promise has no error handling; loadTopicView failure leaves an endless loading state with no error UI

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, the `model(params)` hook returns `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id).then(...)` with no `.catch`/`error` action handling in this route. While Ember will generally route rejected model promises to an error substate, this diff does not add any explicit error UI/handling for this new route, so failures of `loadTopicView` may result in a poor/unhandled user experience. The claim of an “endless loading state” is not directly verifiable from the diff, but the lack of explicit error handling is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url}; any add_unsubscribe_link caller not passing it will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and silently fail email sending

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `unsubscribe_link` (config/locales/server.en.yml) to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` (lib/email/message_builder.rb), when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it unconditionally does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` and inserts it, but `template_args` only includes defaults + `@opts` and does not set any default for `unsubscribe_url`. Therefore any existing caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url` will trigger `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` at runtime. This diff updates one caller (`user_notifications.rb`) and one spec, but the lack of a default/guard in MessageBuilder makes the finding valid as a defect risk introduced by the translation change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 301 permanent redirect for slug canonicalization caches stale mappings; a 302/307 should be used instead

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, when `slugs_do_not_match` (or non-JSON + blank slug), the code does `redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url, status: 301`. A 301 is explicitly introduced here and could cause clients/intermediaries to cache the redirect even if the canonical slug changes later, which is a legitimate behavior/UX concern tied directly to this diff. It’s not a clearly verifiable functional break from the diff alone (it will still redirect correctly), but it is a concrete review issue about redirect semantics for slug canonicalization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Possible template/route naming mismatch: route resolves topicUnsubscribe template but new template is under topic/unsubscribe path, risking a blank page or template-not-found error

adjudication.rationale: The new Ember route is declared as `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' });`, which will resolve (via Ember’s dasherizing lookup) to `route:topic-unsubscribe`/`controller:topic-unsubscribe`/`template:topic-unsubscribe`. The diff adds `routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, and `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, but the template added is `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` (i.e., `template:topic/unsubscribe`), not `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs`. With no `renderTemplate` override shown in `routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, this looks like a real template naming mismatch that could cause a template-not-found/blank render.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New state-mutating endpoint TopicsController#unsubscribe has zero test coverage; no integration test exists for the email link → GET → level downgrade flow

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicUser.find_by returning nil causes NoMethodError on tu.notification_level, giving a 500 to any logged-in user visiting an unsubscribe URL for a topic without a TopicUser record

adjudication_records.issue_text: State-mutating GET unsubscribe link with no token/confirmation: email prefetchers and security scanners will trigger the toggle, and because the action toggles rather than idempotently mutes, repeated prefetches flip-flop notification state unpredictably (config/routes.rb:438-439, app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:95)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Toggle semantics contradict UI copy: clicking the link on a watching/tracking topic only downgrades to regular on the first click, so the user still receives reply/mention emails despite the page saying notifications will stop; either unconditionally mute or update the copy (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:100-106, config/locales/client.en.yml)

However the new UI/email copy claims the action will “stop receiving notifications” / “stop receiving notifications about this particular topic” (config/locales/client.en.yml topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications; config/locales/server.en.yml unsubscribe_link). adjudication_records.issue_text: P1 — Nil dereference in unsubscribe endpoint: TopicUser.find_by can return nil and tu.notification_level is called without a guard, causing NoMethodError/500 error for users without a TopicUser row (e.g., category-watch flows)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and immediately calls `tu.notification_level` without checking `tu` for nil. adjudication_records.issue_text: P2 — State-mutating GET request: the unsubscribe action mutates persistent user state (tu.save!) on a plain GET with check_xhr skipped, enabling CSRF-style abuse via tags and email-scanner bots auto-muting topics before the user clicks

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds GET routes for `topics#unsubscribe` (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" ...`) and implements `TopicsController#unsubscribe` which changes `TopicUser.notification_level` and persists it via `tu.save!`. This is a state-mutating action performed on a plain GET, and the controller explicitly skips `:check_xhr` for `:unsubscribe`, increasing exposure to CSRF-style triggering (e.g., embedded image tags, link prefetchers/email scanners) without any indication of a required authenticity token or POST/PUT method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2 — One click does not fully unsubscribe: watching/tracking users clicking the link are set to 'regular' (still receiving reply/mention emails), while the page claims they will stop receiving notifications; only a second click fully mutes

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the new logic *toggles* topic notification level: if `tu.notification_level > regular` (e.g., tracking/watching) it sets it to `regular`, otherwise it sets it to `muted` (`topics_controller.rb` in the diff). That means a watching/tracking user needs two clicks to reach `muted`. However the new client copy says “You will stop receiving notifications for …” (`client.en.yml` + `topic/unsubscribe.hbs`), and the email copy says “To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, click here” (`server.en.yml`). The behavior (first click only downgrades to regular) doesn’t match the promise of stopping notifications, so the finding is verifiably grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2 — Missing unsubscribe_url interpolation: unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, but only some callers pass it; other email paths using add_unsubscribe_link: true will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument, causing silent email delivery failures in background jobs

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `unsubscribe_link` (server.en.yml) to include `%{unsubscribe_url}` but `Email::MessageBuilder`’s default `@template_args` (message_builder.rb) does not set `unsubscribe_url`; it only merges whatever opts were passed. While `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` is updated to pass `unsubscribe_url`, the diff does not show that *all* other potential `add_unsubscribe_link: true` callers were updated, so this introduces a concrete risk of `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` if any call site omits it. The claim about “other email paths” can’t be fully verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3 — Raw save! bypasses TopicUser.change invariants: no MessageBus publish leaves other sessions stale, and notification_level_changed_at is not stamped, allowing automatic level-recalculation to silently override the user's unsubscribe

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the PR updates `TopicUser` by mutating `tu.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!` directly. The diff shows `TopicUser.change` contains side effects when `attrs[:notification_level]` is set (it publishes a `MessageBus` event: `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, ...)`). By bypassing `TopicUser.change`, this unsubscribe change will not publish the notification-level-change event, so other open sessions/UIs depending on that bus update can remain stale. (The claim about `notification_level_changed_at` cannot be verified from the diff, but the MessageBus invariant bypass is verifiable.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3 — notification_level nil comparison: if the TopicUser row exists with NULL notification_level, tu.notification_level > ... raises on nil comparison, a second crash path alongside the P1 issue

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` and then immediately evaluates `if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]`. If the `topic_users` row exists but `notification_level` is `NULL`, `tu.notification_level` will be `nil` and `nil > Integer` will raise (`NoMethodError`/comparison on nil). The diff itself suggests `notification_level` can be NULL (e.g., `TopicUser.tracking` uses `COALESCE(topic_users.notification_level, :regular)`), so this is a real crash path introduced/exposed by the new action.
